title: NTA UGC NET English Full Mock Test #15
subtitle: 100 Questions · 200 Marks · Post-2018 NTA Pattern · Zero Answer Bias (25 A/B/C/D) · Reading Comprehension (Q91-100)

items.title: Mock #15 · Q1
items.stem:
Match the following technological advancements impacting learning and teaching of language with their corresponding years:
(a) Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) — (i) 2004
(b) Streaming of Video on the Internet — (ii) 2003
(c) MySpace.com — (iii) 1991
(d) Facebook — (iv) 1997
Choose the correct option :
items.explanation: Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) was first publicly released by Tim Berners-Lee in 1991 (a-iii), commercial video streaming on the internet emerged in 1997 (b-iv), MySpace.com was launched in 2003 (c-ii), and Facebook was founded in 2004 (d-i).

items.title: Mock #15 · Q2
items.stem: Which statement among the following rightly defines an 'epithet'?
options: An adjective/adjectival phrase that condemns the protagonist of a story/novel
An adjective/adjectival phrase suited for inscription on a tomb or memorial
An adjective/adjectival phrase used to define a characteristic quality or attribute of some person or thing
A rhetorical figure by which the same word or phrase is repeated at the end of successive lines
items.explanation: An epithet is an adjective or adjectival phrase used to characterize a distinct quality or attribute of a person or thing, such as Homer's 'swift-footed Achilles' or 'rosy-fingered dawn'.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q3
items.stem:
Said identifies Orientalism as :
I. What an Orientalist does.
II. A style of thought based on an ontological and epistemological distinction made between the Orient and the Occident.
III. a discourse dealing with the Orient
IV. a fact of nature rather than one of human production
In the light of the statement above :
options: II and III are correct, I and IV are wrong.
I and III are correct, II and IV are wrong.
I, II and III are correct and IV is wrong.
IV is correct and I, II and III are wrong.
items.explanation: In the Introduction to Orientalism (1978), Edward Said defines Orientalism in three interdependent ways: academically as what an Orientalist does (I), imaginatively as a style of thought based upon an ontological and epistemological distinction between the Orient and the Occident (II), and historically/materially as a Foucauldian discourse for dominating and restructuring the Orient (III), while explicitly rejecting the idea that the Orient is an inert fact of nature (IV).

items.title: Mock #15 · Q4
items.stem: Deductive method of research intends to :
items.explanation: The deductive research method moves from the general to the particular, beginning with a general theoretical framework or hypothesis and testing it against specific empirical observations. In contrast, inductive research moves from particular observations to general conclusions.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q5
items.stem:
Arrange the following novels of D. H. Lawrence in chronological order of their year of publication:-
A. Women in Love
B. The White Peacock
C. Sons and Lovers
D. The Rainbow
E. The Trespasser
items.explanation: D. H. Lawrence's novels in chronological order of publication are: The White Peacock (1911), The Trespasser (1912), Sons and Lovers (1913), The Rainbow (1915), and Women in Love (1920). This sequence corresponds to B -> E -> C -> D -> A.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q6
items.stem:
As Adam and Eve leave Paradise, "hand in hand with wand'ring steps and slow" (Book
XII, Paradise Lost) what is their consolation ?
options: They are comforted by their foreknowledge of the coming of Christ as Redeemer of mankind
They are comforted by their love for one another
They are comforted by God, who travels before them in the form of a pillar of fire
They are comforted by the angel, who holds each of them by the hand
items.explanation: In Book XII of John Milton's Paradise Lost, before Adam and Eve are expelled from Eden, the archangel Michael reveals to Adam the future history of humankind culminating in the incarnation, crucifixion, and resurrection of Christ as Redeemer, leaving Adam and Eve with 'a Paradise within thee, happier far'.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q7
items.meta: Unit IX: Literary Theory Post World War II
items.stem:
Assertion (A) : The act of reading a text is both determinate and indeterminate.

Reason (R) : Since our reading includes both a sense of the unity of the narrative held in place at the end and the different wishes and guesses made along the way.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the true explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the true explanation of (A).
items.explanation: In reader-response criticism (as discussed by Wolfgang Iser and Andrew Bennett & Nicholas Royle), reading a narrative is simultaneously determinate and indeterminate (A) because readers experience both provisional expectations/guesses along the way and retrospective narrative closure at the end (R).

items.title: Mock #15 · Q8
items.stem: Who among the following prose writers of the Romantic period authored "On Murder Considered as one of the Fine Arts"?
items.explanation: Romantic essayist Thomas De Quincey wrote the satirical dark-humour essay 'On Murder Considered as One of the Fine Arts', first published in Blackwood's Magazine in 1827 (followed by a second paper in 1839 and a postscript in 1854).

items.title: Mock #15 · Q9
items.stem:
In the following list, which two actors belong to the Elizabethan period?
(a) Richard Burbage
(b) Will Kempe
(c) David Garrick
(d) John Kemble
Choose the correct option:
items.explanation: Tragedian Richard Burbage (a) and comic actor Will Kempe (b) were both famous Elizabethan performers and key members of Shakespeare's acting company, the Lord Chamberlain's Men. David Garrick and John Philip Kemble were eighteenth-century actors.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q10
items.stem:
In which poem does Judith Wright lament the erasure of native culture in the following
lines ?
"The song is gone; the dance
Is secret with the dancers in the earth,
The ritual useless, and the tribal story
Lost in an alien tale"
items.explanation: These opening lines are from Australian poet Judith Wright's famous 1946 elegy 'Bora Ring' (published in The Moving Image), which mourns the colonial destruction of Indigenous Australian culture and sacred ceremonial grounds.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q11
items.stem:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
LIST-I (Source) | LIST-II (Types of Research Material)
A. Bartleby | I. World's largest bibliographic database
B. Project Muse | II. A repository of theses
C. WorldCat | III. A range of verse and fiction
D. Shodhganga | IV. Full Text research article
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Bartleby.com provides an online archive of classic verse, fiction, and reference works (A-III), Project MUSE is a digital database providing full-text scholarly research articles (B-IV), WorldCat is the world's largest bibliographic database (C-I), and Shodhganga is INFLIBNET's digital repository of Indian PhD theses (D-II).

items.title: Mock #15 · Q12
items.stem:
The basic concept that creation was
ordered, that every species exists in a
hierarchy of status, from God to the
lowest creature, was prevalent in the
Renaissance.
In
this
hierarchical
continuum, man occupies the middle
position between the animal kinds and
the angels.

This world view is known as
items.explanation: The Great Chain of Being (scala naturae) was the classical and Renaissance cosmological worldview holding that all creation is arranged in a strict, divinely ordained hierarchy extending from God and the angels down through humanity (the middle link between spirit and matter) to animals, plants, and stones.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q13
items.stem:
Identify the plays written by Asif Currimbhoy from the following:
A. Princes
B. The Captives
C. An Experiment with Truth
D. Angkor
E. Dance Like a Man
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Indian English dramatist Asif Currimbhoy wrote The Captives (1963, B), An Experiment with Truth (1969, C, on Mahatma Gandhi), and Angkor (1973, D), whereas The Princes (1963) is a novel by Manohar Malgonkar and Dance Like a Man (1989) is a play by Mahesh Dattani.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q14
items.stem:
How would a New Historicist critic interpret Derrida's statement, "there is nothing outside
the text" ?
options: historicist critics should restrict their attention to a culture's literary productions, all other data is irrelevant to the critic's task
language conditions the way we see the world, and there is no reality beyond the 'prison house' of language
there is no meaning outside of textual meaning (contrary to the mimeticist's position)
literature" encompasses all cultural artifacts and all the values, power relations, and ways of seeing reflected in those artifacts; there is nothing outside of the "text" broadly conceived
items.explanation: New Historicist critics such as Stephen Greenblatt interpret Jacques Derrida's dictum 'il n'y a pas de hors-texte' ('there is nothing outside the text') to mean that all historical, social, and cultural artifacts—alongside literary works—form an interconnected web of circulating discourses, power relations, and textualized meanings.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q15
items.stem:
Arrange the following terms in the chronological order as these appeared in literary theory:
 A. phallogocentrism
 B. locutionary act
 C. interpellation
 D. interpretive community
 Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The chronological order of these theoretical terms is J.L. Austin's 'locutionary act' (1955/1962, B), Louis Althusser's 'interpellation' (1970, C), Jacques Derrida's 'phallogocentrism' (1973–74, A), and Stanley Fish's 'interpretive community' (1976/1980, D).

items.title: Mock #15 · Q16
items.stem:
Which of the following statements is
not
true
of
Laurence
Sterne's
Tristram Shandy ?
options: It opens and ends with the theme of birth
It contains a trip to France
items.explanation: Laurence Sterne's The Life and Opinions of Tristram Shandy, Gentleman (1759–67) is famous for its radically non-linear, digressive narrative structure rather than a linear plot; it also features a marbled page, a journey through France, and comic preoccupations with conception and birth.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q17
items.stem:
Assertion (A) : In the 1950s and 60s Baldwin and Ellison returned to universal themes and focused on innovations in literary forms.
Reason (R) : In the 1930s and 40s African and American Literature was mostly pre-occupied with protest.
In the light of the above two statements, choose the correct option :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
items.explanation: In the 1950s and 1960s, James Baldwin (in essays like 'Everybody's Protest Novel') and Ralph Ellison (in Invisible Man) consciously moved away from the sociological protest naturalism of the 1930s–40s (exemplified by Richard Wright) toward formal innovation and universal human complexity.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q18
items.stem:

English

the survey of English poetry

evangelism in English poetry
III.
contemporary literary scene

items.explanation: Lord Byron's heroic-couplet satire English Bards and Scotch Reviewers (1809), provoked by Henry Brougham's harsh review of Hours of Idleness, provides a critical survey of English poetry (I) and attacks the contemporary Romantic literary scene and Edinburgh reviewers (III).

items.title: Mock #15 · Q19
items.stem:
Which of the following statements are true with regard to Postcolonial theory and literature?

A. The Empire Writes Back is a non-fictional text on postcolonialism

B. Black Skin White Masks is a fictional text narrating multidisciplinary analysis of the effects of colonialism on the protagonist

C. A Cntique of Postcolonial Reason is a work written by Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak

D, Edward W. Said wrote his autobiography titled In Place to reflect the love-hate relationship with the West

E. Postcolonialism addresses those questions that emerge in the wake of the departure of colonial masters

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: Statements C and E are true: Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak authored A Critique of Postcolonial Reason (1999), and postcolonialism critically investigates questions and cultural legacies following the departure of colonial rulers. Statement B is false because Frantz Fanon's Black Skin, White Masks is a non-fictional psychological critique; and Statement D is false because Edward Said's memoir is titled Out of Place (1999), not In Place.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q20
items.stem: Abt Vogler is authored by
items.explanation: 'Abt Vogler' is a dramatic monologue by Robert Browning published in Dramatis Personae (1864), in which the eighteenth-century German composer and organist extemporizes on his musical instrument and meditates on artistic permanence.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q21
items.meta: Unit V: Language: Basic Concepts, Theories and Pedagogy
items.stem:
Match the column:
A. Pidgin
B. Creole
C. Idiolect
D. Register
I. The language special to an individual, sometimes described as a ‘personal dialect’.
II. A language defined according to social use, such as scientific, formal, religious, and journalistic.
III. A contact language which draws on elements from two or more languages
IV. A term relating to people and languages especially in the erstwhile colonial tropics and subtropics, in the Americas, Africa, the Indian Ocean, and Oceania.
items.explanation: These sociolinguistic terms match their definitions: a pidgin is a contact language drawing on two or more languages without native speakers (A-III), creole designates contact languages nativized in colonial plantation regions (B-IV), an idiolect is an individual's unique personal speech variety (C-I), and a register is a variety determined by social and functional domain (D-II).

items.title: Mock #15 · Q22
items.stem: Francis Bacon's New Atlantis is about a utopian state called __________
items.explanation: Published posthumously in 1626, Francis Bacon's unfinished utopian prose romance New Atlantis depicts the mythical Pacific island kingdom of Bensalem, centred on its state-sponsored scientific research institution, Salomon's House.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q23
items.stem:
Which two of the following features shall apply to Roland Barthes’s notion of a ‘writerly text’?
(A) In case of writerly text, the reader accepts the meaning without too much reading effort
(B) A writerly text tends to focus attention on what is written
(C) A writerly text makes the reader a producer
(D) A writerly text tends to be self-conscious.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: In S/Z a writerly text makes the reader a producer of meaning, and it is self-conscious about its own writing. A readerly text is the one read passively.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q24
items.stem: Who wrote the book The History of European Languages?
items.explanation: Scottish philologist Alexander Murray (1775-1813) wrote The History of European Languages; or, Researches into the Affinities of the Teutonic, Greek, Celtic, Sclavonic, and Indian Nations, published posthumously in 1823.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q25
items.stem:
What is the correct chronological sequence of the following English non-fictional prose writers according to their years of birth?
A. Joseph Addison
B. Francis Bacon
C. Charles Lamb
D. Virginia Woolf
E. Matthew Arnold
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The birth years of these non-fictional prose writers are: Francis Bacon (1561, B), Joseph Addison (1672, A), Charles Lamb (1775, C), Matthew Arnold (1822, E), and Virginia Woolf (1882, D), giving B, A, C, E, D.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q26
items.stem:
Pope's The Rape of the Lock was
published in 1712 in
items.explanation: Alexander Pope's mock-heroic poem The Rape of the Lock was first published anonymously in May 1712 in Lintot's Miscellaneous Poems and Translations in two cantos (334 lines), before Pope expanded it in 1714 into its final five-canto version.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q27
items.stem:
Assertion (A) : In so far as we are taught how to read, what we engage are not texts but
paradigms.

Reason (R)
: We appropriate meaning from a text according to what we need or
desire, or, in other words, according to the critical assumptions or
predispositions that we bring to it
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
items.explanation: Both statements are drawn from feminist critic Annette Kolodny's landmark essay 'Dancing Through the Minefield' (1980). Kolodny argues that reading is a learned activity governed by interpretive paradigms (A) because readers extract meaning according to the critical assumptions and predispositions they bring to a text (R).

items.title: Mock #15 · Q28
items.stem: The author of the book observes "I have attempted, through the medium of biography, to present some Victorian visions to the modern eye". The four main characters in this book are Cardinal Manning, Florence Nightingale, Dr. Arnold and General Gordon. Who is this author ?
items.explanation: In the Preface to Eminent Victorians (1918), Bloomsbury biographer Lytton Strachey wrote this statement to introduce his ironic, debunking biographical portraits of four revered Victorian figures: Cardinal Manning, Florence Nightingale, Dr. Thomas Arnold, and General Charles Gordon.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q29
items.stem:
Which of the following are the plays written by Robert Greene?
A. The Famous Chronicle of King Edward the First
B. Alphonsus
C. A Moon for the Misbegotten
D. The Old Wives' Tale
E. King of Aragon
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: University Wit Robert Greene wrote the blank-verse play Alphonsus, King of Aragon (c. 1587, split here into B 'Alphonsus' and E 'King of Aragon'). The Famous Chronicle of King Edward the First and The Old Wives' Tale are by George Peele, and A Moon for the Misbegotten is by Eugene O'Neill.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q30
items.stem: Gaiutra Bahadur wrote an autobiographic novel titled
items.explanation: Guyanese-American writer Gaiutra Bahadur authored Coolie Woman: The Odyssey of Indenture (2013), an autobiographical and historical account tracing her great-grandmother Sujaria's 1903 journey from colonial India to British Guiana.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q31
items.stem:
Match the column:
(Novel)
A. The Childhood of Jesus
B. The Go-Between
C. Brideshead Revisited
D. The Catcher in the Rye
(Novelist)
I. L. P. Hartley
II. Evelyn Waugh
III. J. M. Coetzee

items.explanation: J. M. Coetzee wrote The Childhood of Jesus (2013) (A-III); L. P. Hartley wrote The Go-Between (1953) (B-I); Evelyn Waugh wrote Brideshead Revisited (1945) (C-II); and J. D. Salinger wrote The Catcher in the Rye (1951) (D-IV). This matches A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q32
items.stem: Which of the following best summarises the structural approach to literature?
options: Meaning is inherent in the word itself.
Meaning is generated through relationships in a system of signs.
A language’s history explains how it works.
Binary oppositions are to be avoided at all costs.
items.explanation: Structuralism in literary studies, developed from Ferdinand de Saussure's linguistics, asserts that meaning does not exist independently within isolated words or objects, but is produced through differential relationships and codes within a larger system of signs.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q33
items.stem:
Which statements are true about Chaucer's The Canterbury Tales?
A. The General Prologue describes the meeting of twenty-nine pilgrims in the Tabard Inn.
B. "The Parson's Tale" is the introductory tale that deals with seven virtues
C. The Canterbury Tales is written in prose and verse of various metres
D. Only twenty-three pilgrims tell stories and there are only twenty four stories told altogether.
E. "The Prioress' Tale" tells about the murder of a mother by a child.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: In Geoffrey Chaucer's The Canterbury Tales, the General Prologue introduces twenty-nine pilgrims at the Tabard Inn in Southwark (A), the collection combines verse in various metres with two prose tales (C), and twenty-three pilgrims tell twenty-four stories in total (D). 'The Knight's Tale'—not 'The Parson's Tale'—opens the collection, and 'The Prioress's Tale' depicts the murder of a Christian choirboy, not a mother; thus A, C, D only.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q34
items.stem: Gabriel Garcia Marquez's postscript to The General in His Labyrinth (1991) about Simon Bolivar's last and terrible journey to the Caribbean coast of Nueva Granada in 1830 is one of the finest examples of _________.
options: processing archival information for theoretical judgement.
reading archive and using its contents.
irrelevance of archive for an artist.
a novelist getting misguided by the archive.
items.explanation: In his 'My Thanks' postscript to The General in His Labyrinth (1989; English trans. 1990), Gabriel García Márquez recounts his exhaustive two-year archival investigation into Simón Bolívar's letters, memoirs, and historical documents, exemplifying how a novelist reads an archive and transforms its contents into fiction.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q35
items.stem:
Arrange the following works of Criticism chronologically:
A. More than Cool Reason
B. Death is the Mother of Beauty
C. Margins of Discourse
D. Meter in English: A Critical Engagement
E. The Rule of Metaphor
items.explanation: These critical works on metaphor and poetics were published in the following sequence: Paul Ricoeur's *The Rule of Metaphor* (E, 1975), George Lakoff and Mark Turner's *More than Cool Reason* (A, 1989), Barbara Herrnstein Smith's *On the Margins of Discourse* (C, 1978), Mark Turner's *Death is the Mother of Beauty* (B, 1987), and David Baker's *Meter in English: A Critical Engagement* (D, 1996).

items.title: Mock #15 · Q36
items.stem:
Matthew Arnold’s “touchstones” were “short passages, even single lines” of classic poetry
beside which the lines of other poets may be placed in order to detect the presence or absence
of high poetic quality.  In his “Study of Poetry” Arnold cited “touchstones” from such
non-English poets as Homer and Dante and also from the English poets, Shakespeare and
Milton.  Which English poet did he disapprovingly call “not one  of the reat classics” in the
list below ?
items.explanation: In 'The Study of Poetry' (1880), Matthew Arnold praised Homer, Dante, Shakespeare, and Milton as high classic poets, but famously judged Geoffrey Chaucer as lacking 'high poetic seriousness', concluding he was not among the supreme classics.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q37
items.stem:
Assertion (A) : In The Power and the Glory, Greene shows how the Whisky Priest transcends his weakness for drink and his human fears, moving towards martyrdom.
Reason (R) : Transcendence in Greene's novels is generally an outcome of love for humanity, but pride is also an essential ingredient in the Priest's character.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation for (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation for (A).
items.explanation: In Graham Greene's novel The Power and the Glory (1940), the unnamed 'whisky priest' overcomes his alcoholism and fear to accept martyrdom in anti-clerical Mexico out of humble compassion and love for humanity rather than pride; per the Official UGC Key, Option (C) is marked.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q38
items.stem:
Thou wilt not wake
Till I thy fate shall overtake;
Till age, or grief, or sickness must
Marry my body to that dust
It so much loves; and fill the room
My heart keeps empty in thy Tomb.
Stay for me there; I will not fail
To meet thee in that hollow Vale.
And think not much of my delay;
I am already on the way.

Which of the following readings do you find appropriate to the spirit of the lines above ?
options: Ageing and dying are of course helplessly passive; but here love makes them as though they were now also willing things in the husband eager to join his dead wife. Through simple intimate tones of their shared earthly life - stay for me, wait for me, I will not fail - he not only imagines her but imagines her thinking of him.

In that interspace between the lines, the ending of one and the beginning of another, there is a silent internal language, the poem's language-within-language, tacitly signalled through the deployment of rhymed space.

The lyric voice here can feel the poem speaking back to him - in the cold lineal stare of 'there was nothing in my belief' - even as his dead wife did not. It is as though the poem itself then demands his response, in order to be able to move from one line to another. To attempt that movement in keeping the poem's space alive, the lyric voice asserts, 'I will not fail/To meet there in that hollow Vale.'

My whole nature was so penetrated with grief and humiliation of such considerations, that, even now, famous and caressed and happy as I am, I often forget in my dream that I have a dear wife who died, leaving me alone in this world. Even that I am a man, and now I wander desolately back to that time of our lives when my wife and I shared moments of bliss.
items.explanation: These lines are from Henry King's famous elegy 'The Exequy' (written on the death of his young wife Anne Berkeley in 1624). Love transforms the helplessness of ageing and death into a willing, eager journey to be reunited with his deceased wife in the grave ('Stay for me there; I will not fail / To meet thee in that hollow Vale').

items.title: Mock #15 · Q39
items.stem:
Which two of the following poems are by Judith Wright?
A. "Meditation on a Bone"
B. "Imperial Adam"
C. "Woman to Man"
D. "The Old Prison"
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: 'Woman to Man' (1949, C) and 'The Old Prison' (D) are celebrated lyrics by Australian poet Judith Wright, whereas 'Meditation on a Bone' and 'Imperial Adam' were written by A.D. Hope.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q40
items.stem:
Thomas Carew's Poems appeared in print in 1640 and contain a variety of amorous

items.explanation: Cavalier poet Thomas Carew's posthumous collection Poems (1640) contains numerous courtly love lyrics addressed to a fictional mistress named Celia, including 'A Rapture' and 'Ask me no more where Jove bestows'.

(2) Wives and Daughters

items.title: Mock #15 · Q42
items.stem: How does Women in Love open ?
options: Rupert Birkin, Lawrence's alter ego, is taking a walk in the English Countryside
The Brangwen sisters, Ursula and Gudrun, are "working and talking
The wedding party gathers at shortlands, the Criches's home
The last lesson is in progress, "peaceful and still" in Ursula's classroom
items.explanation: D. H. Lawrence's novel Women in Love (1920) opens in Chapter 1 ('Sisters') at the Brangwen home in Beldover, where the sisters Ursula and Gudrun Brangwen are sitting together 'working and talking' about marriage before walking to the Crich wedding.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q43
items.stem:
Which two of the following dramatists have won the Sultan Padamsee Award?
A. Mahesh Dattani
B. Gurcharan Das
C. Girish Karnad
D. Cyrus Mistry
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Gurcharan Das (B) won the inaugural Sultan Padamsee Award for Playwriting in 1968 for his historical play Larins Sahib, and Cyrus Mistry (D) won the Sultan Padamsee Award in 1978 for his play Doongaji House.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q44
items.stem:
The statement 'I think, therefore, I
am' is by
items.explanation: The foundational rationalist proposition 'I think, therefore I am' (Je pense, donc je suis / Cogito, ergo sum) was formulated by French philosopher René Descartes in his Discourse on the Method (1637) and Principles of Philosophy (1644).

items.title: Mock #15 · Q45
items.stem:
Arrange the following chronologically in accordance with their date of birth:

A. Goethe
B. Oscar Wilde
C. Bertolt Brecht
D. Eugene O'Neill
E. Moliere

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Dramatists and writers by year of birth: Molière (1622, E), Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (1749, A), Oscar Wilde (1854, B), Eugene O'Neill (1888, D), and Bertolt Brecht (1898, C).

items.title: Mock #15 · Q46
items.stem: Marvell's "The Coronet" seeks to explore the human condition in terms of the conflict between
items.explanation: In Andrew Marvell's devotional poem 'The Coronet,' the speaker attempts to weave a floral garland of poetic praise for Christ, only to find the serpent of mortal pride and artistic vanity coiled within it, illustrating the conflict between fallen human nature and divine grace.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q47
items.stem:

items.explanation: American analytic philosopher John Searle famously attacked Jacques Derrida's deconstructive reading of J. L. Austin's speech-act theory ('Signature Event Context') in his 1977 essay 'Reiterating the Differences: A Reply to Derrida', prompting Derrida's lengthy rejoinder in Limited Inc (1988).

Mr. Sampath is by R. K. Narayan and Dopdi Mejhen is the protagonist of Mahasweta Devi's 'Draupadi'.

items.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore wrote the celebrated plays Sacrifice (Visarjan, 1890), Muktadhara (The Waterfall, 1922), and Chandalika (1933), whereas Eknath is the name of a 16th-century Marathi Bhakti saint-poet and not a play by Tagore.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q52

items.explanation: These lines are from Percy Bysshe Shelley's sonnet "To Wordsworth" (published in 1816), in which Shelley laments William Wordsworth's political abandonment of republican and revolutionary ideals in favor of political conservatism.

items.explanation: In English, a three-consonant cluster at the start of a syllable (as in 'split', 'street', 'screen') always begins with /s/, followed by a stop and then a liquid or glide.

C. Niyataapti (Certainty of success)
D. Yatna (Effort)
E. Phalaagama (Attainment of the result)
items.explanation: In Sanskrit dramaturgy, Dhananjaya's Dasharupaka defines the five successive stages of dramatic action (avasthas): Arambha (Beginning, B), Yatna (Effort, D), Praptyasha (Prospect of Success, A), Niyatapti (Certainty of Success, C), and Phalagama (Attainment of the Result, E). items.explanation: In Euripides's Greek tragedy Medea (431 BC), set in Corinth where Jason and Medea live in exile, the Chorus consists of fifteen Corinthian women who are Medea's sympathetic neighbours and confidantes as she confronts Jason's betrayal.

items.explanation: William Hazlitt formulated this famous appraisal in his introductory lecture 'On Poetry in General' in Lectures on the English Poets (1818), asserting that poetry is not a mere profession but the very essence, passion, and vitality of human existence.

Poetry, as a mania – one of Plato’s two higher forms of “divine” mania – has, in all its species, a mere insanity incidental to it, the “defect of its quality”, into which it may lapse in its moment of weakness; and the insanity which follows a vivid poetic anthropomorphism like that of Rossetti may be noted here and there in his work, in a forced and almost grotesque materialising of abstractions, as Dante also became at times a mere subject of the scholastic realism of the Middle Age.
— Walter Pater

In Rossetti, the forced personifications may be
(A) an incidental defect of poetic quality
(B) examples of a madness of thought
(C) an exaggerated concretisation of things
(D) a divinely inspired poetic expression
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
items.explanation: Pater calls the forced personifications a 'defect of its quality' (A) and a 'grotesque materialising of abstractions' (C). Marked doubtful because options 1 and 3 repeat the same pair.

Read the following passage and answer questions
I do entreat your grace to pardon me.
I know not by what power I am made bold,
Nor how it may concern my modesty,
In such a presence here to plead my thoughts;
But I beseech your grace that I may know
The worst that may befall me in this case,
If I refuse to wed Demetrius.
—A Midsummer Night’s Dream

Who is the speaker of the above lines?
items.explanation: Hermia speaks these lines to Duke Theseus in Act 1, Scene 1, when she refuses to marry Demetrius.

items.title: Mock #15 · Q99
items.meta: Unit IV / Unit VIII: Prose & Criticism
items.stem:
Read the following and then answer the questions that follow
He went to work in this preparatory lesson, not unlike Morgiana in the Forty Thieves: looking into all the vessels ranged before him, one after another, to see what they contained. Say, good M’Choakumchild. When from thy boiling store, thou shalt fill each jar brim full by-and-by, dost thou think that thou wilt always kill outright the robber Fancy lurking within – or sometimes only maim him and distort him.
—Dickens, Hard Times

In the expression “... looking into all the vessels ranged before him...”, which one of the following devices is used?
items.explanation: The children are described as vessels to be filled, which is a metaphor, since no 'like' or 'as' is used.
